lead.hed: Howard's gunner's mates walked the crew through the M240 in the northern Pacific
lead.insight: DVIDS posted Friday a Navy photo of Chief Gunner's Mate Dalton Daniel explaining how an M240 machine gun works to the small-caliber action team on the starboard bridge wing of the destroyer USS Howard. The ship was operating in the northern Pacific. The caption, dated Oct. 14, says Howard is forward-deployed with Destroyer Squadron 15, the Navy's largest destroyer squadron and 7th Fleet's principal surface force. The photo was taken Oct. 13 and posted Oct. 16.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Matt Riggs · DVIDS 10024071 · Public domain · Chief Gunner's Mate Dalton Daniel explains an M240 to the small-caliber action team aboard USS Howard (DDG 83) in the northern Pacific. Photo taken Oct. 13, 2026; posted Oct. 16.

political.hed: Heritage says the Trump-Xi summit bought time and kept leverage
political.insight: Friday's Heritage report covers Chinese General Secretary Xi Jinping's Sept. 23–25 visit to Washington for a summit with President Donald Trump. An earlier Heritage analysis had expected tactical agreements, not a breakthrough. The report says the outcomes that followed bought time and preserved American leverage.

political.hed: American Reformer says America is reacting to a global order coming apart
political.insight: Friday's American Reformer essay says the plates of the global order have been shifting since the 2010s and have not settled. It argues that blaming Donald Trump and MAGA misses the point: in most respects they are reacting to events, not controlling them. American power is real, the piece says, and still not enough to hold a system that is coming apart.

political.hed: The Navy turned six flag billets over to civilians and cut six more to captain
political.insight: USNI News reported Thursday that the Navy changed six billets held by flag officers into civilian posts, following Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's call for fewer generals and more troops. The service identified 14 flag billets in the review and reduced six of those to captain.

tech.hed: Defense News says the order to slow Starshield for Ukraine came from the White House
tech.insight: Defense News, citing Reuters, reports that two U.S. officials and a Western official said the order to limit SpaceX's Starshield service for Ukraine came from inside the White House. Defense Department leaders were told the service needed to be slowed. The officials did not name who decided. Ukrainian officials said military-grade terminals stopped working on fast-moving objects, which hit drones that use them for guidance. A Ukrainian Defence Ministry person said Thursday the terminals were working again in motion, but only up to 100 miles per hour.

tech.hed: Special Operations is fielding a half-mask and goggles instead of a full respirator
tech.insight: Defense News reports that the Pentagon and Avon Protection announced a contract on Oct. 9 for the MITR half-mask and goggle system. Avon says it is meant to guard against chemicals, lead powder from gunfire, and substances such as fentanyl, and that it does not replace a full-face respirator. The goggles and mask can be worn together or apart. Avon said some elite units are already wearing it. The story ties the buy to a November 2025 SOF Cancer Study that found special-operations personnel face an 18 percent higher cancer risk than other personnel. The photograph with the story is a company image, not an official still.

culture.hed: WORLD reports the Muellers still have no grave for Kayla
culture.insight: WORLD reports that Carl and Marsha Mueller wrote President Donald Trump on Nov. 6, 2025, before his meeting with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, asking for help bringing their daughter home. ISIS took Kayla Mueller hostage in Syria on Aug. 4, 2013, and reported on Feb. 6, 2015, that she had been killed. The couple told WORLD they have no grave and no marker. The Foley Foundation told WORLD that at least 38 American citizens are held by terror groups or hostile governments, and that two recent hostages, Robert Gilman and Kevin Rideout, came home in August.

culture.hed: WORLD follows a Liberty runner whose kratom habit ended in a Richmond detox call
culture.insight: WORLD reports that Cameron Francis, then a distance runner at Liberty University, started mixing a green powder into his water as a junior, looking for a plant-based alternative to alcohol. In an emergency room in 2021, a doctor told his father, Dean Francis, that the powder was akin to an opioid. When Dean called a detox center in Richmond, Virginia, where the family lives, the person on the line equated kratom with heroin. WORLD says eleven states and dozens of cities have banned it, and that the FDA does not approve selling it. It is still sold online and in convenience stores, smoke shops, and health-food stores.

watch.hed: Musk says Starshield is a government system and Starlink is not for offensive use
watch.note: Defense News, citing Reuters, reports that Elon Musk posted Wednesday that Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government, and that limits on speed or usage are decided by the U.S. military or the president. He said Starlink is a commercial SpaceX service limited to civilian or defensive use. The same piece says Starlink is a network of more than 11,000 satellites with about 13 million subscribers. The photograph with the story is a news-agency image, not an official still.
